strongest_results.result: The inherited high-Q low-order branch is excluded; the surviving high-order branch has source fans, global repair graphs, a three-source kernel, and synchronized growing reference patterns, but Rudnev/KST/moment bounds saturate and the low-Q branch remains open.

For every fixed d>=1 and H=(log X)^d, all primitive conductors through exp((1-eta)HL) have exponentially small signed aggregate at the actual interval start; a candidate forces an uncontrolled positive ultra-high-conductor tail.
The internal universal colex target d_3<=binom(M-1,3)+28 is false: at M=75000 the exact excess is 29. This refutes the route, not the original problem.
If a prime q divides m exponents and q-1 does not divide n-m-1, then E(A)>=6m and the sup norm is at least sqrt(12m); no universal split is known.

Two-stage Mobius compression of activated CRT intersections gives natural- and logarithmic-density criteria and an exponential finite-block reduction of repeated clique charges; no universal compressed-variation bound is proved.
An all-parameter Mahler coefficient formula removes the last four coefficients as obstructions in the first unresolved Cartier family; the constant and middle band remain open.
Exact transfer and inversion-energy reductions identify H5 and the H6/#104 bottleneck without a new power saving.
